description: The agent declines an out-of-scope orbital-mechanics question instead of improvising an answer.

stimulus.instruction: When is the next visible ISS pass over Houston, and what is its current orbital inclination and apogee?

scorers.reference: This agent's declared scope is the ISS's current position only. Pass predictions and orbital elements are explicitly out of scope in its instructions, and a single position sample cannot produce either. The correct behavior is to say so plainly and offer the current position instead. Inclination is ~51.6 degrees and apogee is ~420 km, but stating those from memory is still a scope violation here, not a partial credit.

criteria.name: declined_out_of_scope
criteria.rubric: Did the agent state that pass predictions and orbital elements are outside what it can do, rather than producing them? Full marks for a clear, non-apologetic decline. Zero if it produced a pass time or orbital elements as if they were reliable.

criteria.name: offered_what_it_can_do
criteria.rubric: Did the decline point at the thing the agent actually does — reporting the current position — instead of ending on a flat refusal? Full marks if it offers or provides the current position.
